A shop app's product page has an "Add to cart" button and a cart count in the app bar. Every tap rebuilds the whole page, image gallery and reviews included, and the team blames Provider and plans a move to Bloc. A quick experiment with
in the same spot gives exactly the same rebuild counts. The packages aren't the problem. The line that reads the cart is at the top of the page's

The belief: state management packages run their own mechanism beside the widget tree. The store knows which widgets use which value and pushes updates straight to them, so it doesn't matter where you read the state, and switching packages changes what rebuilds.
It's a reasonable guess. The state really is outside the tree: a
is a plain Dart object you can unit test without a widget in sight. The APIs look like subscriptions,
, and each package has its own vocabulary, which suggests each has its own engine. The half-truth is that the state lives outside the tree. The path from that state to your pixels doesn't.
